items.title: DoorDash Air: Drone Delivery Goes Mainstream
points: DoorDash obtained FAA Part 135 air carrier certification (federal approval allowing a company to operate its own commercial aircraft/drone fleet), enabling its own drone delivery fleet
Drones will handle mid-distance deliveries (3-5 miles), while human Dashers keep shorter, more complex routes
Fleet averaged 25-minute deliveries during 2025 testing
Demo video drew 1.4M views, signaling market readiness

items.title: Robot Adoption Faces Economic Barriers Despite Technical Capability
points: Anthropic study: current robots can technically handle physical tasks making up 34% of US working hours, mostly in controlled settings like warehouses, and could technically perform 74% of physical tasks overall
Driving and warehouse jobs face highest displacement risk; nursing and repair work remain relatively protected due to complexity and variability
Robots are cheaper than human workers for only 0.3% of tasks today, a figure projected to reach just 10% within 40 years
Labor cost, not technical capability, is the main barrier to wider robot deployment

items.title: Humanoid Robots Score Marketing and Capability Wins
points: Figure AI's F.02 humanoid robots autonomously walked into a 75-ton molten steel vat at a Finnish foundry to securely destroy retired hardware, avoiding manual teardown
The stunt (reportedly suggested by Arnold Schwarzenegger) generated 1.8M social media views, boosting Figure's profile in the humanoid robot race
Dyna Robotics' Taku robot completed an hour-long, uncut demo: loading/unloading washers, folding towels, sorting laundry by size, and restocking shelves with no human help
This full-workflow success hints at near-term automation potential for hotels and laundromats

items.title: Military and Commercial Robotics Expansion Accelerates
points: Pentagon created an Autonomous Warfare Command to scale AI, drones, and robotics across US military operations
Amazon announced $100M+ investment in an Indiana manufacturing hub (by 2028) to boost warehouse robotics production
Tesla reportedly builds hundreds of Optimus humanoid robots weekly, but most stay in internal testing due to reliability and generalization issues
MIT engineers built a wafer-thin robot using living muscle cells and light-based steering, pointing toward softer robot designs for delicate aquatic tasks

items.title: SpaceX Starbase Drone Cleanup Ahead of Starship Flight 14
points: A drone cleaned the SpaceX Starbase launch facility ahead of Starship Flight 14
Flight 14 became the first Starship mission to sustain orbit and deploy operational satellites
